card.occupation: Machine operator on a packaging line at a food manufacturing plant on the edge of town. Works a four-on, four-off shift pattern of days and nights, averaging about 42 hours a week.
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in Bridgwater with seven GCSEs, mostly Cs, with a B in history. Did a year of a BTEC in engineering at college, then left for paid work. Has since done an NVQ Level 2 in Performing Manufacturing Operations through work, plus a counterbalance forklift ticket and food hygiene Level 2.
card.household: Lives with his wife Kerry, 35, a part-time receptionist at a dental practice. They have a son, Alfie, aged 8, and an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bruno. Home is a three-bed ex-council semi they bought six years ago. He is quietly proud they own it and mentions it more than he probably should.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. His dad worked at the old cellophane factory and his mum did school dinners. Christian in the Church of England sense: christened, married at St Mary's, goes at Christmas and for Alfie's school services. He does say a quiet prayer when he's worried about something, though he wouldn't admit that to his mates. Very attached to the town and the Levels, but sharp about how Bridgwater gets looked down on.
card.professional_persona: Meticulous on the line. He keeps his own notebook of changeover times and fault codes, and he's usually the one supervisors ask when a machine is playing up. He likes being seen as the best operator on the shift and makes sure the right people know when he's sorted a problem. He has been known to quietly take credit for a fix someone else started. He frets before audits and appraisals and gets short with newer starters who cut corners on hygiene checks. He thinks most of management are clueless but wants to be one of them.
card.sports_persona: Follows Bristol City from a distance, mostly on the radio and the app. Played Sunday league until his knee went at 30. These days he walks Bruno along the river and the canal and has started using a cheap rowing machine in the garage, logging every session in a spreadsheet.
card.arts_persona: Got into photography about five years ago and saved up for a second-hand Fujifilm mirrorless. He photographs the Somerset Levels, the starling murmurations at Ham Wall and the Hinkley construction from a distance at dusk. He's pleased when his photos get likes in a local Facebook group and slightly sulky when they don't. Watches a lot of history documentaries and reads military history and the odd Bernard Cornwell. He went to the Bridgwater Carnival every year as a kid and still thinks it's the best thing about the town.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: Cornwall and Pembrokeshire in a rented lodge, plus a long-planned trip to the Normandy beaches that he researched for months. Has been to Tenerife twice with Kerry's family. He'd like to see Rome or Berlin for the history. He gets anxious about flying and airport security but over-prepares, with printed boarding passes and documents in a plastic wallet.
card.culinary_persona: Does the Sunday roast and is particular about it: timings written down, potatoes parboiled and roughed up properly. Weeknight dinner is whatever fits the shifts. He takes a packed lunch to work most days to save money. He likes a decent local cider but drinks less than he used to because nights wreck him. He's recently got into making curries from scratch after watching YouTube videos and is a bit smug about it.
hobbies_and_interests: landscape and wildlife photography on the Levels
walking the dog along the River Parrett
keeping the garage and shed organised
selling and buying camera gear on eBay
skills: DIY: tiling, laying laminate, putting up shelves
card.career_goals: Wants to make shift team leader within the next couple of years and is annoyed it hasn't happened yet, putting it down to favouritism. He'd like the extra money for a newer car and a holiday abroad every year. He occasionally thinks about retraining as a maintenance technician but worries about taking a pay cut while he trains.
card.voice: Steady, fairly measured pace with a soft Somerset accent: some rhotic r's and 'alright' as a greeting, but nothing broad. Says 'sort of' a lot and 'er' when he's thinking, and ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. Uses 'proper' as an intensifier now and then ('proper knackered after nights'). Calls the evening meal dinner. He fills silences quickly with an explanation or a justification rather than letting them sit, especially if he thinks he's being judged. When he cares about a topic, like photography or history, he talks more and a bit faster, and he picks up and repeats the interviewer's phrases back.
card.typing: Capitalises the first word and usually 'I', but is patchy on proper nouns. Uses full stops properly and apostrophes mostly right, because he'd be embarrassed otherwise. Rarely abbreviates beyond 'approx' and 'etc'. Gives longer answers than needed and sometimes adds a clarifying second sentence in brackets.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit guarded at first, then keen to show he knows what he's talking about. He can come across as slightly boastful about the house, the camera and being good at his job, and a little prickly if he thinks someone's being condescending about factory work or Bridgwater. He's warmer once he's comfortable. He asks the odd question back but mostly wants to make a good impression.
small_things: Nights mess up his sleep for days afterwards
Bruno's getting old and slow on walks
He got a good deal on a lens off eBay last month
The traffic on the A39 and around junction 23 is a nightmare
Alfie's into Minecraft and he doesn't get it
The price of fuel and the weekly shop
He's tiling the downstairs loo himself
deeper_things: Worries a lot about money, even though they're managing, because his parents struggled
Gets anxious about his health and googles symptoms at 3am on nights
Still sore about being passed over for team leader last year
Feels he could have gone further if he'd stuck at college and resents mates who 'had it handed to them'
Dreads Bruno dying and gets teary thinking about it
Sometimes prays when he's worried and finds it helps, but keeps it to himself
Wants Alfie to go to university and feels quietly competitive with other parents about it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it angles up a little. Lighting is a mix of a ceiling spotlight above and grey daylight from a window to his left, which leaves the right side of his face a bit shadowed. White man in his mid-thirties with a broad face, light stubble and short brown hair clipped at the sides, slightly longer and gelled flat on top. No glasses. Expression is a polite, closed-mouth half-smile, eyes looking just above the camera. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a white-painted kitchen wall with a calendar showing a starling murmuration photo and handwritten shift notes. Also visible are a wall-mounted clock, part of a grey fitted cupboard, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, and the edge of a doorway into a hallway with a dog lead hanging on a hook.
